h: Football, snow and a bouncy Manchester weekend
p: Inflatable parks reward a bit of preparation. Smaller children often get on best in the quieter, younger-age sessions some parks run, while older kids and adults will want the full, fast-paced experience. It's worth checking what's on offer when you book, along with any height or age rules for the bigger slides. Pop a towel and spare top in the car, because the combination of air-filled obstacles and enthusiastic racing gets everyone surprisingly sweaty.

Manchester is football country, and both of the city's big clubs offer stadium tours, so a morning of bouncing followed by a peek behind the scenes at Old Trafford or the Etihad makes a properly memorable day for young fans. The National Football Museum sits right in the city centre and is packed with shirts, trophies and interactive challenges where you can test your own penalty-taking.

If you're still craving adventure after the inflatables, Chill Factore near the Trafford Centre has real indoor snow for skiing, snowboarding and sledging, a fun contrast to an hour of bouncing. For something gentler, Heaton Park in north Manchester is a huge green space with a grand hall, woodland walks, a boating lake and play areas. The Metrolink tram network connects much of the city and its suburbs, which makes getting between all of these a lot easier than battling city traffic. Wherever you end up, the curry houses of the Curry Mile in Rusholme are a classic Manchester way to refuel a starving family after a day of bouncing and exploring.
